text.arabic_uthmani: فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ ذَنُوبًۭا مِّثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحَٰبِهِمْ فَلَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ

words.gloss_range: consequential connective opening the verdict from the prior proof and narrative sequence
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) does not start a free-standing sentence; it carries the preceding proof and destruction catalog into a verdict. Its payoff is architectural: the ayah opens as consequence, and the earlier flight-command conclusion (51:50) is answered here by a consequence of judgment.

topics.headline: prior proof becomes verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse begins as a consequence of what came before, not as an isolated threat.
topics.reason: The opening particle links the allocation clause to the preceding narrative and makes the first beat consequential.

topics.headline: earlier command answered by verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a local surah arc: the earlier command to flee (51:50) now has a verdict-shaped counterpart.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply concrete links to the earlier fa-command and the immediately prior divine attribute declaration.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle governing the allocation clause, with the delayed subject still under its force
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) locks the whole allocation under emphasis even though the recipient phrase is fronted and the subject arrives later. The word makes the verdict sound already settled: the syntax delays disclosure of the portion, but not the certainty of the claim, and it carries the prior assertion into this allocation.

topics.headline: emphasis governs the whole allocation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the punishment portion is presented as emphatic settled news, not tentative prediction.
topics.reason: The particle scopes over the full nominal allocation clause and combines with the opening consequence.

topics.headline: fronting delays the named portion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the recipients before the allotted portion, so attention lands first on who is being judged.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the prepositional recipient phrase as fronted predicate and the portion noun as delayed ism.

topics.headline: assertion carries across the boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices continuity from the prior assertion into this one; divine self-description is not left detached from the verdict.
topics.reason: The boundary row and emphasis rows converge on assertion carrying from the previous statement into the allocation.

words.gloss_range: preposition of assigned possession or recipient; here the allotment is for them in an adverse sense
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) marks the wrongdoers as the assigned recipients of the portion, and the fronting makes that assignment the first thing heard inside the emphatic clause. Its twist is adverse possession: what is for them is not a benefit but a claim against them, with the tiny preposition bound directly to the relative class it targets.

topics.headline: fronted assigned recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause prioritizes the judged recipients before naming the portion itself.
topics.reason: The preposition heads the fronted predicate and marks the recipient or possessor of the allotted portion.

topics.headline: for them becomes against them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the preposition carrying a reversal: possession here means liability rather than favor.
topics.reason: The local verdict gives the possession value an adverse direction without changing the preposition into a separate lexical item.

topics.headline: preposition binds to the relative class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the short preposition is phonologically and syntactically tied to the class it targets.
topics.reason: The particle is inseparable from the following relative phrase in the local recipient construction.

words.gloss_range: masculine plural relative pronoun defining the recipient class by the following act of wrongdoing
words.prose: {{ar:لَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:lladhīna}}) makes the recipients a defined class rather than a named tribe. The following clause supplies the criterion, so the verdict reaches whoever fits the wrongdoing description; the formulaic breadth survives, while the local grammar keeps the class anchored to this ayah.

topics.headline: identity routed through wrongdoing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that identity is defined by the act that follows, not by ancestry or name.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun introduces the clause that defines the recipients of the allotted portion.

topics.headline: formulaic class beyond one group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the wording can classify all who match the wrongdoing formula, while the local referent remains the wrongdoers under discussion.
topics.reason: The recurring formula supports class breadth, but attachment evidence keeps the local antecedent inside the recipient frame.

topics.headline: relative phrase depends on the preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the relative class is already grammatically installed before the allotted portion appears.
topics.reason: The surface is governed by the preceding preposition and fronted before the delayed portion noun.

words.gloss_range: completed active wrongdoing in a relative clause, left absolute without an overt object
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes wrongdoing, injustice, misplaced action, and darkness; the local verb selects completed wrongdoing while those fields sharpen the condemnation
words.prose: {{ar:ظَلَمُوا۟}} ({{tr:ẓalamū}}) gives the class its criterion as completed active wrongdoing, with no object supplied for the wronging. The root {{ar:ظ ل م}} ({{tr:ẓ-l-m}}) lets injustice, misplacement, and darkness sharpen the label, while the local verb stays a perfect relative-clause act. It also ties the verdict to the surah pattern: earlier rebellion (51:44), measured portion, likeness, and the later haste-demand all meet under the wrongdoer classification.

topics.headline: completed wrongdoing defines the class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict is attached to completed agency, not vague moral atmosphere.
topics.reason: The perfect active verb in the relative clause supplies the criterion for the recipient class.

topics.headline: objectless verb broadens the charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that no object limits the wronging; the act functions as an absolute class marker.
topics.reason: Verb-instance evidence marks the frame as objectless absolute, matching the CRITICAL claim.

topics.headline: injustice and darkness color the label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that wrongdoing carries a darkening and misplacement field, while the local sense remains moral wronging.
topics.reason: The root field enriches the condemnation, but local Form I perfect does not activate every branch as a separate sense.

topics.headline: wrongdoing links to measured consequence and haste
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the wrongdoer label is structurally tied to the portion, equivalence, and haste-demand that follow.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows identify local and distributional links between wrongdoing, portion vocabulary, likeness, and hastening.

topics.headline: specific rebellion becomes general label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prior rebellion scene (51:44) is generalized into a juridical class in this verdict.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah and boundary rows tie this label to the surrounding surah movement without changing the local grammar.

words.gloss_range: an allotted portion under emphasis; local sense is share or portion, with sin-language and bucket-measure imagery coloring it
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes sin, consequence, tail, and bucket-like apportioned share; the local noun selects the allotted portion while keeping accountability pressure
words.prose: {{ar:ذَنُوبًۭا}} ({{tr:dhanūban}}) is the delayed subject of the emphatic clause, so the hearer first receives the judged class and only then the allotted share. The root {{ar:ذ ن ب}} ({{tr:dh-n-b}}) makes the portion feel measurable, like a drawn allotment, while the sin-field keeps it morally accountable; local syntax selects a punishment share, not a bare sin. Its marked form makes the share feel weighty, and its sound leans into the coming comparison as the prior provision frame (51:58) turns into punitive allocation.

topics.headline: delayed unspecified allotted share
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the portion is withheld until after the recipients are foregrounded, then introduced as an unspecified allotment.
topics.reason: The noun is the delayed ism of the emphatic particle, accusative and indefinite.

topics.headline: bucket-share and sin field converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices punishment as a measured share drawn from the same root field as sin, while local grammar selects the share sense.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL polysemy is useful, but the local noun phrase functions as an allotted portion rather than simply the offense itself.

topics.headline: marked form magnifies the portion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the non-default form as weightier than a plain sin-word, though size language should remain qualitative.
topics.reason: The form and rarity support marked portion language, but the bundle does not require a fixed quantitative translation.

topics.headline: first half of the portion equation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this first portion is not complete by itself; it opens an equation with the later precedent portion.
topics.reason: The first occurrence is specified by the following comparison and mirrored by the second occurrence.

topics.headline: sound prepares comparison and provision turns punitive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices both texture and placement: the word audibly leans into comparison and turns the prior provision frame (51:58) into punitive allocation.
topics.reason: The rows connect sound, root rarity, prior provision, and calibrated allocation without requiring a new lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: comparison noun specifying equivalence between the new portion and the precedent portion
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes likeness, counterpart, parable, exemplary treatment, and standing forms; the local noun selects equivalence or counterpart measure
words.prose: {{ar:مِّثْلَ}} ({{tr:mithla}}) is the hinge of equivalence: it restates the new portion by measuring it against a precedent portion. The root {{ar:م ث ل}} ({{tr:m-th-l}}) can range into parable and exemplary treatment, but here the local construct selects exact counterpart measure; the punishment is not merely similar, it is calibrated as the like of what came before.

topics.headline: portion specified as equivalence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first portion is immediately specified by a measure, not left vague.
topics.reason: The noun functions as apposition or adjective to the portion and governs the precedent portion in construct.

topics.headline: likeness becomes exact counterpart measure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices equivalence rather than loose resemblance, while broader parable or punishment branches stay secondary.
topics.reason: The local syntax and comparison noun support exact measure; broader root branches color but do not replace the selected sense.

topics.headline: parable field becomes enacted verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a parable-like root field turned into an actual verdict, while the local word still means counterpart measure.
topics.reason: The rows about parable and exemplary punishment survive as coloring of the equivalence, not as a separate translation sense.

topics.headline: middle term binds repeated portions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the word as the center of the equation between the present allotment and the precedent allotment.
topics.reason: The structural rows all point to the comparison word as the pivot between the two portion terms.

words.gloss_range: genitive precedent portion governed by the comparison noun and bound into the construct chain
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes sin, consequence, tail, and bucket-like apportioned share; the local genitive noun selects the precedent portion in the comparison
words.prose: {{ar:ذَنُوبِ}} ({{tr:dhanūbi}}) is the precedent side of the equation, arriving late as the known template after the comparison has been set up. The root {{ar:ذ ن ب}} ({{tr:dh-n-b}}) still carries measured allotment and accountability, but the genitive construct now makes the share known by attaching it to the companion group. The repeated word changes case and role, turning the present portion and the prior portion into a visible equivalence.

topics.headline: precedent portion under comparison
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second portion is not a new allotment but the known precedent by which the first is measured.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive under the comparison word and supplies the precedent quantity.

topics.headline: portion bound to the companions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the precedent portion is inseparable from the group whose fate supplies the template.
topics.reason: The construct state and following genitive companion term bind the portion into the double idafa chain.

topics.headline: measured bucket image as historical template
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same measured-share image now functioning as a historical template, while local syntax still selects precedent portion.
topics.reason: The bucket-share field is retained as imagery but constrained by the genitive comparison construction.

topics.headline: same word, different case, equation made audible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated term doing different grammatical jobs while equating present and past shares.
topics.reason: The accusative first occurrence and genitive second occurrence mirror each other around the comparison word.

topics.headline: historical template arrives late
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase withholds the known template until after the comparison has been set up.
topics.reason: The rows describe the second portion as completing and delaying the equivalence structure.

words.gloss_range: construct plural with possessive suffix naming the counterpart group whose portion sets the template
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes companionship, possession, association, and shared condition; the local construct selects the counterparts or fate-sharing group
words.prose: {{ar:أَصْحَٰبِهِمْ}} ({{tr:aṣḥābihim}}) completes the double construct chain by naming whose precedent portion counts. The root {{ar:ص ح ب}} ({{tr:ṣ-ḥ-b}}) makes the group more than social companions: they are counterparts and fate-sharers, linked back by the suffix to the present wrongdoers and back through the surah to earlier rejecters (51:52). Its closing position seals the verdict beat before the warning turns.

topics.headline: companions complete the measure phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the comparison phrase resolves only when the companion group is named.
topics.reason: The noun is the final genitive in the double construct chain and completes the measurement architecture.

topics.headline: suffix binds present to prior counterparts
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the companions are theirs; the present group is grammatically tied to its predecessors.
topics.reason: The possessive suffix resumes the wrongdoer group and binds it to the comparison template.

topics.headline: companionship becomes shared fate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices companionship as a fate-sharing category, not merely ordinary company.
topics.reason: The root range and local punishment context let companion, possessor, and fellow-fate-sharer converge.

topics.headline: prior people-of groups become the template
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that earlier destroyed communities become the current wrongdoers counterpart class.
topics.reason: The rows connect the word to prior community language, including people-of formulas (15:78, 26:176, 15:80) and the nearby prior-peoples frame (51:52).

topics.headline: final word seals the first beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first beat closing on historical counterparts before the ayah pivots to warning.
topics.reason: The position, definitizing suffix, plural shape, and collocations all support this word as the closure of the verdict beat.

words.gloss_range: consequential connective pivoting from the settled verdict into the closing warning
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) turns the ayah from settled allocation into warning. It keeps the closing clause dependent on the verdict rather than floating as general advice: because the portion has been declared, the hastening demand is blocked. The repeated fa pattern gives the ayah a two-step logic: verdict, then prohibition or negated warning.

topics.headline: consequence scopes the warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warning follows from the portion already assigned.
topics.reason: The second connective introduces the verbal warning clause as a consequence of the verdict beat.

topics.headline: conjunction anchors the closing clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final warning is not independent moral advice but the practical implication of the allocation.
topics.reason: The conjunction joins the negated or prohibitive clause to the previous allocation.

topics.headline: paired fa markers form two-step logic
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated particle pattern: first consequence becomes verdict, then verdict becomes warning.
topics.reason: The two fa markers organize the ayah into verdict and consequent prohibition.

topics.headline: pivot opens two readings of the warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pivot introduces a clause that can be heard as prohibition or as negated statement.
topics.reason: The following particle and imperfect allow both prohibitive and negational parsing.

words.gloss_range: negative or prohibitive particle scoping over the hastening verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is the switch that turns the hastening verb into the blocked action. Because the following form does not visibly separate jussive from indicative, the warning can be heard both as a command not to demand haste and as a statement that they cannot hurry the speaker. That ambiguity makes the clause threatening rather than merely descriptive.

topics.headline: negative particle governs the hastening verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices exactly where the ayah blocks the demand: the negation or prohibition falls on seeking haste.
topics.reason: The particle scopes over the following verb and opens the warning clause.

topics.headline: prohibition and negation remain live
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices two simultaneous forces at the same surface: stop demanding haste, and you will not hasten it.
topics.reason: The verb form with protective nūn and object ending obscures the usual mood contrast, preserving both readings.

topics.headline: prohibition answers an actual demand
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the prohibition as a response to mockingly requested punishment, which makes it a threat.
topics.reason: The prohibitive reading presupposes the behavior being addressed and functions as warning after the verdict.

words.gloss_range: Form X imperfect with first-person object suffix; local sense is seeking or demanding haste from the speaker
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes haste, immediacy, quick provision, calf terminology, and premature action; the local Form X selects seeking or demanding acceleration
words.prose: {{ar:يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ}} ({{tr:yastaʿjilūni}}) closes the ayah on a resisted demand, not on neutral impatience. The root {{ar:ع ج ل}} ({{tr:ʿ-j-l}}) supplies haste and immediacy, with the calf-root recurrence (51:26) coloring the demand for the immediate while the local Form X makes the wrongdoers seek acceleration and the final object suffix makes the speaker the target. The same surface still carries command-or-statement ambiguity; the surah has already named their hastening demand (51:14), and now the final word leaves that pressure blocked against the firm divine identity just declared (51:58), with a closure that can linger against the speed it names.

topics.headline: same form supports command or statement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing can forbid their demand and also deny their ability to accelerate it.
topics.reason: The imperfect after the negative or prohibitive particle can be read as jussive or indicative in this surface form.

topics.headline: the demand targets the speaker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demand is not general impatience; it is directed at the speaker as the one they try to hurry.
topics.reason: The final first-person object suffix, protected by nūn al-wiqāya, supplies the target of the request.

topics.headline: seeking haste rather than being hasty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the wrongdoers as agents soliciting acceleration, not merely people with a hasty temperament.
topics.reason: The Form X construction and local object make the act a request or demand for haste.

topics.headline: immediacy field colors the demand
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a broader immediacy field, including the calf-root recurrence (51:26), while the local verb remains seeking haste.
topics.reason: Root-family evidence can color the immediacy theme, but unrelated noun branches do not replace the local Form X sense.

topics.headline: wrongdoers demand accelerated punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the closing verb as part of the Quranic pattern where wrongdoers press for the punishment they deny.
topics.reason: The rows tie the haste verb to wrongdoing, the earlier same-surah demand (51:14), and the explicit demand formula at 38:16.

topics.headline: final position and long ending resist haste
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah ending on the attempted acceleration itself, with recitation texture that can linger on the object.
topics.reason: The final position, long ending, and qiraat closure variants all affect how the blocked demand lands.

topics.headline: haste runs into divine firmness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the demanded acceleration set against the divine firmness and identity declared just before (51:58).
topics.reason: Boundary and variant rows preserve the speaker-target relation and contrast the haste demand with the prior divine description.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ذَنُوبًا مِثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحَابِهِمْ فَلَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ
baseline_models.mechanism: The repeated dhanub is an allotted share; mithl calibrates parity, ashabihim supplies the associated cohort, and the closing prohibition blocks pulling that allocation ahead of its time.

activation_trace.role: Putting something outside its proper place supplies the culpable displacement that makes the allocation consequential.
The share or lot image makes both repeated nouns a matched allocation rather than an unspecified consequence.
Similarity and equalization calibrate one share against the other.
Adherence and companionship define the cohort to which the wrongdoers' allotment corresponds.
Seeking a thing before its time makes the final clause a ban on advancing the allotted consequence.

changed_reading.before: Wrongdoers face a consequence like that of their companions.
changed_reading.after: Wrongdoers already stand under a parity-calibrated allotment matching the cohort with whom their wrongdoing associates them, but its delivery is not theirs to advance.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: ذَنُوبًا مِثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحَابِهِمْ فَلَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ
baseline_models.mechanism: A full bucket, an irrigation or lifting apparatus, paired equality, and accompaniment converge on a measured draw taken by turns; haste becomes an attempt to pull one's assigned draw forward.

activation_trace.role: The full-bucket image materializes each repeated dhanub as a filled measure.
The irrigation and lifting apparatus supplies the mechanism by which a filled measure is drawn and moved.
Equal matching makes the two bucket-measures commensurate.
Making one thing accompany another supplies the paired allocation of measure to cohort.

changed_reading.before: Dhanub denotes an abstract penal share and the wrongdoers should not demand it early.
changed_reading.after: The clause also supports a material analogy of equal filled draws assigned to successive cohorts, with haste pictured as interfering with the order of drawing.

baseline_models.mechanism: The tail, ending, and follower branches of dhanb combine with companionship and equality: the wrongdoers can be read as trailing adherents whose comparable end follows the cohort they continue.

activation_trace.role: The tail and ending image turns the share into an end that comes behind what precedes it.
Followers attached to leaders supply a diachronic relation between current wrongdoers and a prior cohort.
Continuing adherence makes the companions a shared-pattern cohort, not necessarily only present associates.
Matching binds the followers' end to the end of those they trail.

changed_reading.before: Ashabihim names the wrongdoers' contemporaneous associates.
changed_reading.after: Ashabihim can name a transhistorical cohort they follow: adherence reproduces the pattern, and a matching end arrives at the tail of that succession.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier assigned time and respite, followed immediately after the focus by a promised day, turn the ban on haste into a fixed schedule for the matched allotment rather than an indefinite postponement.

activation_trace.role: The share image supplies the item whose delivery is temporally governed.
Seeking before the proper time is the temporal action revised by the context.
Assigning a known time supplies a bounded interval before consequence.
Waiting and granting respite make delay an active allowance rather than absence of outcome.
A defined duration gives the warning a temporal container.
A promise fixed to a time or place identifies the endpoint governing the preceding no-haste clause.

structural_cues: 51:44 places seizure after defiance and within a scene of watching.
51:60 immediately names the day they are promised.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an assigned interval, respite, a bounded day, and a timed promise; I infer that these cues govern the focus prohibition and schedule its allotment. A live alternative is that each timing cue belongs only to its local episode and the focus uses delay rhetorically.

changed_reading.before: Do not hurry the punishment because it has merely been deferred.
changed_reading.after: Do not try to advance a matched share whose interval and promised endpoint are already fixed; respite is scheduled, not cancellation.

context_deltas.mechanism: Precedence, the same circulating accusation, and the image of one thing being linked or passed to another turn the focus companions into a diachronic cohort whose recurring response is followed by a recurring allotment.

activation_trace.role: Followers attached to preceding leaders make the present wrongdoers the trailing members of a repeated pattern.
Adherence defines companionship by participation in the same response across time.
Matching connects repeated conduct to a corresponding repeated share.
Precedence places the earlier peoples ahead of the focus wrongdoers in a temporal sequence.
A saying spread among people supplies the recurring verbal pattern shared by separated cohorts.
Linking one thing to another makes the rhetorical transmission question a mechanism of historical continuity.
Mutual passing of an injunction sharpens the image of cohorts handing on one response.

structural_cues: 51:38-46 presents successive peoples and successive consequences.
51:52 explicitly compares the present response with those before them.
51:53 asks whether the cohorts transmitted the response to one another.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies prior cohorts, the same saying, precedence, and a transmission link; I infer that ashabihim can span time and that matched conduct generates matched allotment. The live alternative is resemblance without transmission, with ashabihim restricted to contemporaries.

changed_reading.before: The wrongdoers receive what their immediate associates received.
changed_reading.after: The wrongdoers join a transmitted historical cohort: they trail the same response and therefore inherit a share matching earlier adherents.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the focus, apportioned provision and sustenance establish a one-way distribution from the self-sufficient provider; the focus dhanub then reads as a dark counter-allotment, a measured share rather than something supplied to God.

activation_trace.role: The share or lot image lets dhanub enter the adjacent distributive frame.
The full measure supplies a material container for the counter-allotment without replacing the penal sense.
An apportioned gift establishes distribution while the verse denies that any such gift is demanded from them.
Sustenance and livelihood specify the provisioning domain that the focus reverses.
Repeated apportioned giving fixes the direction of distribution with God as giver immediately before the penal share.

structural_cues: 51:57 denies that God seeks provision or feeding from them.
51:59 immediately assigns the wrongdoers a dhanub.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacent apportioned provision, sustenance, a giver-to-recipient direction, and focus branches for share and full measure; I infer a deliberate distributive reversal in which punishment is an anti-provision. The alternative is a simple contrast with no shared allocation mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The wrongdoers possess an abstract portion of punishment.
changed_reading.after: Their portion is framed as a measured counter-provision dispensed by the one who needs nothing from them: not sustenance they give, but an allocation they receive.

context_deltas.mechanism: Proper pairing is followed by the prohibition against assigning another deity alongside God; the focus then reverses misplaced association by locating valid equality not at the divine level but between wrongdoers and the shares of their real cohorts.

activation_trace.role: Putting something in the wrong place supplies the error of assigning equivalence where it does not belong.
Equality returns as a correctly placed correspondence between penal shares.
Association identifies the actual peers among whom correspondence holds.
A counterpart joined to its counterpart supplies the section's legitimate pairing frame.
Assigning a thing a status supplies the act by which a false counterpart is positioned.
Worship and the worshipped object specify the relation in which the prohibited equivalence is made.
Otherness after a first marks the rival term placed alongside God.

structural_cues: 51:51 forbids making another deity with God.
51:59 uses equality and companionship only for matched penal shares.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies proper counterparts, a prohibited assigned deity, focus misplacement, and focus equality; I infer a retributive reversal from false equivalence to correctly located equivalence. The alternative is that the pairing and deity prohibition do not govern mithl in the focus.

1. **A full bucket becomes an allotted punitive share.** `ظ ل م/B008` supplies withholding rights; `ذ ن ب/B007` a large/full water bucket and B006 an allotted portion; `م ث ل/B001` likeness; `ص ح ب/B001` associates; `ع ج ل/B001` hastening. The doubled *dhanūb* and comparison distribute matching bucket-shares across associated groups. I infer **shared wrong-pattern -> matched allotment of consequence**. The water-drawing image turns judgment into taking one's measured turn.
2. **Culpable consequence follows its companions.** `ذ ن ب/B001` supplies sin and bad consequence, while `ص ح ب/B001` supplies sustained association. The historical sequence supplies the companions whose outcomes form the model. I infer **association in conduct -> likeness in consequence**. This ethical reading coexists with the concrete bucket/share mechanism.
3. **Haste cannot alter queue or measure.** `ع ج ل/B001` supplies seeking before the proper time. Because the share is already likened and allotted, I infer **premature demand -> no acceleration of assigned turn**. The prohibition answers 51:12-14 and preserves appointment rather than uncertainty.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 51:60 names the assigned turn as “their day,” closing the bucket/share image with an appointed temporal possession.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **A measured bucket of consequence arrives on its own schedule.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed `ظ ل م/B004` is “doing something at the wrong concrete time or place”; repeated fixed `ذ ن ب` activates `B007`, “tail-handled full bucket,” and `B006`, “portion or allotted share”; fixed `م ث ل/B001` is likeness; `ص ح ب/B001` close association; fixed `ع ج ل/B001` hastening. **Structural cue:** blame has been lifted from the messenger, reminder remains beneficial, creation has a worship-purpose, and God is the nondependent Provider (51:54–58); only the promised day follows (51:60). **Role and abduction:** the bucket materializes an allotment, likeness matches it to associated predecessors, and haste tries to pull that measured draft out of time; I infer that wrong placement generates a correspondingly scheduled portion. **Reading change:** `ذنوب` becomes a distributive container-image: consequence is drawn as a full assigned share, so demanding acceleration cannot alter its measure.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişi ya da şeyle geçici olmayan biçimde birlikte bulunmak, ona eşlik etmek veya onunla yakınlığını sürdürmektir. Belirli yapılarda bir şeyin sahibi ya da sorumlusu olmayı ve kişinin yanında bir eşlikçi bulunmasını da anlatır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek, iki tarafın yakın ve süreğen biçimde birlikte bulunması ya da birinin ötekine eşlik etmesidir.
Eşlik eden taraf kişi, hayvan, yer veya zamanla ilişkili olabilir; tekil eşlikçi ve eşlikçiler topluluğu da adlandırılabilir.
Belirli ad tamlamalarında bir şeyin sahibi, ona bağlı kişi veya onun işini yürüten sorumlu kastedilir.
Bir kişinin yanında kendisine eşlik eden birinin bulunması da bu anlam alanının yapıya bağlı uzantısıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir işte tez davranmak, bir şeyi ya da kişiyi çabuklaştırmak, isteneni vaktinden önce aramak veya vermek, başkasının önüne geçmek ve geciktirilmiş olmayana yönelmek.

facets.statement: Bir işte yavaş davranmanın karşıtı olarak hızla ve beklemeden davranmadır.
Bir başkasını hızlandırma, bir işi erkene çekme veya bir şeyi vaktinden önce isteme ilişkisini kapsar.
Geciktirilmiş olana karşı elde bulunanı ve bir şeyin önüne geçmeyi de anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çerçevesi tez davranma ile yavaşlığın karşıtlığını temel alır; buna hızlandırma, vaktinden önce isteme, öne geçme ve geciktirilmemiş olma anlamları eklenir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi ortak çekirdeği çabuk hazırlanıp sunulan, kolay yenilen veya hızla götürülen yiyecekte kurar; yol azığı, çobanın getirdiği süt, konuklara önceden sunulan yemek ve küçük yiyecek parçaları bunun türleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal genel tezlik anlamı değildir; yiyecek ve azıkla sınırlı adlar ile bir yolcu söz öbeğini kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın yiyecek adları ile yalnız yolcunun kolay yiyeceği azığı anlatan söz öbeği ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Çabuk hazırlanıp sunulan, kolay yenilen veya hızla eve götürülen yiyecek ve azık; yolcunun hurma benzeri yiyeceği, çobanın sütü ve konuklara hazırlık bitmeden sunulan yemek bunun özel biçimleridir.

facets.statement: Hazırlanması, sunulması veya yenmesi hızlandırılmış yiyecek ya da azıktır.
Yolcunun kolayca yediği hurma ve kavrulmuş tahıl gibi yol yiyeceğini belirtir.
Çobanın ailesine hızla götürdüğü sütü veya konuklara hazırlık tamamlanmadan sunulan yemeği anlatır.
Kurutulmuş süt ürünü, hurma veya bunların karışımından yapılmış küçük uzun parçalar da bu adla anılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar çabuk elde edilen veya kolay yenilen yiyecek çekirdeğinde birleşir; yol azığı, eve götürülen süt, hazırlıksız konuğa sunulan yemek ve hurma ya da kurutulmuş süt ürünü parçaları bu kapsamı örnekler.

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.
